newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to assume $13 oil price in 1997/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to assume $13 oil price in 1997/98 budget.

text.p: Kuwait has assumed a $13 per barrel price for its crude oil in a preliminary budget plan for the 1997/98 fiscal year (July-June), Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan said in remarks published on Thursday.
The budget calculations are based on an exchange rate of 0.300 dinar to the dollar, Rodhan told al-Qabas newspaper.
State spending in the 1997/98 budget would be 4.3 billion dinars ($14.3 billion) according to preliminary estimates, said Rodhan without disclosing a deficit forecast figure.
Projected spending in the 1996/97 budget stands at 4.21 billion dinars with a deficit of 1.21 billion.
The $13 per barrel price is unchanged from the assumption in the 1996/97 and 1995/96 budgets.
Crude oil of the type exported by Kuwait has been selling at about $5 over the estimated price helping Kuwait to slash its budget deficit, economists say.
Kuwait has reduced its deficit for 1995/96 to 653 million dinars from a projected 1.32 billion.
A member of the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), Kuwait produces 2.0 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil.
